capacity_workload.name: tensor_network_single_device_capacity_v1
capacity_workload.premise_established_note: A capacity premise requires one measured shape that exhausts a single device and that a sharded run completes at the same frozen slicing. No such shape was measured on this pair, and the reason is recorded rather than assumed: for every shape measured so far the per-rank peak is identical at world size 1 and at world size 2 to within a few megabytes. The reverse-mode peak fell from 80.93 GiB at two sliced labels to 51.19 GiB at four and then stopped responding to slicing, and the pair reproduces that same number rather than halving it. A pair run therefore demonstrates that the training update is sharded -- each rank owns half the slice tasks and writes back only its own parameters -- but not that the pair trains a workload one device cannot, because the allocation that exhausts the device is not owned by any single slice. The slicing this contract freezes is one of the measured rungs, and at that rung the single device completes: the frozen grid at four sliced labels runs to completion on one device at 51191433216 bytes. The contract therefore does not describe an exhaustion at all, which is why the baseline cannot be recorded from it and why the ladder rung that does exhaust a device, two sliced labels at 80930380288 bytes, is recorded as a measurement rather than promoted into the freeze.

single_gpu_baseline.rationale: The single-device capacity failure is read as provenance evidence rather than as a release-gate payload, for the same reason the statevector lane reads it that way: a single device cannot shard one logical workload across ranks, so no world_size 1 artifact can satisfy the release gate. It is read from results_path rather than from benchmarks/results/scalability because the strict promotion audit requires every file in that directory to be release-grade sharded scalability evidence.

freeze_note: This manifest freezes the tensor-network release protocol and records that its capacity premise is not yet established. Four capacity candidates were falsified by measurement rather than by argument. First, flagquantum_18q_13l_expectation was frozen as the premise of an earlier campaign and then completed on a single A800 in 14.296 s at a 0.70 GiB peak, so it cannot be the workload one device fails to train. Second, the 24-qubit and 28-qubit grid ladder that replaced it does not separate the two cases either: the reverse-mode peak is not slice-owned above four sliced labels, so every measured shape that exhausts one device also exhausts both devices at the same peak. Third, the pair does not halve the peak for any measured shape, including the ones that exhaust a single device, so a pair run of a failing shape fails in the same place and at the same number of bytes. Fourth, the slicing this contract itself freezes does not exhaust a device: the measured ladder records the frozen 4x6x2 grid at four sliced labels completing on one device at 51191433216 bytes, so the capacity-failure producer refuses this contract with 'the frozen capacity workload completed on a single device, so it is not a capacity premise and cannot be recorded as one' instead of recording an exhaustion that did not happen. The ladder is recorded under capacity_workload.measured_ladder and capacity_workload.premise_established is false, because a premise declared rather than measured is not evidence. The gate therefore reports capacity_premise_not_established rather than passing on an assumed premise, and the capability stays at production_supported until a measured shape separates a single-device failure from a sharded completion. The speed protocol is frozen here so that the part of the release that does not depend on the premise can still be measured at one revision.

speed_workload.freeze_note: The timing protocol is two warmup and ten measured iterations rather than the statevector lane's five and thirty, because one tensor-network step is a complete forward and reverse contraction over the sliced network and takes orders of magnitude longer than one statevector training step at a comparable width. The protocol is frozen before the run and the acceptance configuration is the widest point of each frozen multiset.
speed_workload.name: tensor_network_matched_speed_v1
speed_workload.timing_unit: one full forward-and-reverse training step over the sliced network
speed_workload.measured_single_device_floor_note: The frozen ladder was measured on one A800 before any release payload was sealed, and the measurement falsifies its own acceptance configuration. The two narrower rungs complete: 84 trainable angles at 0.79 GiB peak in 15.0 s, and 128 at 8.53 GiB in 30.4 s. The acceptance configuration the freeze names, 180 trainable angles over eighteen wires and ten layers at six sliced labels, exhausts the device: it peaks at 66.9 GiB and then asks for a further 16 GiB, which does not fit on an 80 GiB accelerator. The pair does not rescue it, for the reason the capacity ladder already records: the rung fails on both ranks with the same 58.9 GiB resident and the same 16 GiB refused, so the reverse-mode peak is not slice-owned and adding a second host does not shrink it. The acceptance configuration is therefore unrunnable on this pair in either mode, and no matched-speed baseline or pair leg can be recorded from it. This is recorded rather than corrected: re-freezing the ladder now, after the measurement, would make the manifest describe a protocol chosen to fit the hardware it was measured on, and the freeze exists to prevent exactly that. The finding is the reason the tensor-network lane holds at production_supported instead of release_certified.

topologies.note: The measured cluster is one pair of hosts, so the release topology is a pair: two ranks, one device each, one on each host. No third host exists here, which is why the frozen topology is a pair rather than a ladder, and why the pair-only boundary is disclosed as a permanent limitation of the capability rather than as a stage of its measurement.
